🚨 A Big East coach just said he's 𝗡𝗢𝗧 recruiting a single high school player this year.

🏀 Kevin Willard (Villanova): six players can come back for a fifth year, so he's keeping them.

💰 John Calipari (Arkansas): "Nine of my players make more than my assistants."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗸𝗶𝗱:
➡️ Rosters are capped and filling with fifth-year players and transfers
➡️ Coaches spend money on 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗻 players
➡️ Spots for high school recruits are getting 𝗳𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 and 𝘀𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗿 (not impossible)

✅ 𝗗𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗼𝗱𝗮𝘆: count the seniors at your child's position on a program's roster, then ask how many could return for a fifth year.

Full breakdown coming on my YouTube channel.

👇 Want to start this process on the right foot? Comment 𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗧 and I'll send you the details on the Parents Recruiting Survival Guide.

Stop Guessing Your Way Through College Recruiting

🏀 The recruiting process is not random. It's structured, and most families don't find that out until it's too late.

After 31 years inside college athletics, I've watched hundreds of families go through this process. The ones who succeed aren't always the most talented. They're the most prepared.
Inside this video I break down why so many talented athletes miss real opportunities, not because of ability, but because their families didn't understand how the system actually works.

📋 I created the College Recruiting On-Ramp System to fix that. It's a coach led education and parent led implementation program that gives your family a real plan instead of a guessing game.

👉 Ready to move from confusion to clarity? 
Link in bio or visit KeithMondillo.com to check out the On-Ramp System.

𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴. It doesn't have to be. 🎯

31 years as an NCAA Director of Athletics and Head Women's Basketball Coach. Thousands of recruits evaluated. Countless conversations with parents who felt stuck and unsure what to do next.

I help families cut through the noise and build a real plan for the recruiting process. Coach communication. Scholarships. Campus visits. NCAA rules. Finding the right fit, not just the biggest name.

📘 Start with my free 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗝𝘂𝗺𝗽𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗣𝗮𝗰𝗸. Four guides. Zero cost. Everything you need to start building your plan today. 👇

🚨 Then grab 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁'𝘀 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲: 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝟱 𝗖𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗹 𝟵𝟯% 𝗼𝗳 𝗙𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀. It's the mistake-proof guide every recruiting parent needs before the process even starts.
Link in bio 👆

👉 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 the word 𝗦𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗘 and we’ll send you the free 𝟭𝟬 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗱

🏀 Misericordia University president 𝗗𝗮𝗻 𝗠𝘆𝗲𝗿𝘀 wrote in Inside Higher Ed on October 26 that Division III should reject five years of eligibility. His line: “We keep the student in front of the athlete.”

Here are his five reasons:
❌ Cost, because Division III has no athletic scholarships
❌ Academic integrity
❌ Competitive imbalance
❌ Displacement of younger players
❌ Transfers from Division I players who already hold degrees

His school has substantial graduate programs, and he still opposes the change.

🎥 In the video, I also share the two concerns I keep hearing:
✅ 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗱𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝘀, because schools without them worry about losing players after four years
✅ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝟭𝟵 𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿, because an older recruit could lose a year or two before he ever enrolls

📋 Whatever Division III decides, you still have to run your own process. Is your family 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆? The scorecard is 10 yes or no questions and takes about five minutes. You also get a free seven-day parent action plan.

👉 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗘 and we’ll send it to you free.

👉 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 the word 𝗦𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗘 and we’ll send you the free 𝟭𝟬 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗱

🏀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗮𝗹 𝟮 goes to a vote at the Division III NCAA convention in January. It would replace four seasons in 10 semesters with 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝘃𝗲-𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗼𝘄.

Here is what it says:
✅ The clock starts at first full-time enrollment or the school year after the 19th birthday, whichever comes first
✅ Pregnancy, active duty military service, and official religious missions pause the clock
✅ It applies to athletes who first enroll full-time in 2027-28 or later
✅ Division I and Division II already adopted the same model

⚠️ There is pushback. The Division III Management Council wants more time to study what Division I and Division II did. On Tuesday, the President’s Council took no position and backed sending the proposal back for more study.

📋 Whatever Division III decides, you still have to run your own process. Is your family 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆? The scorecard is 10 yes or no questions and takes about five minutes. You also get a free seven-day parent action plan.

👉 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗘 and we’ll send it to you free.

👉 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗯 your free 𝟭𝟬 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗱. It’s in my bio, or visit KeithMondillo.com

🏀 Division I and Division II give athletes 𝗳𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 to play. Division III gives four. This January, Division III schools vote on whether to change that.

If your child is headed to a Division III school, this vote matters. It decides how much time they get to grow into their sport.

🎥 In this video, I cover:
✅ What the proposal says
✅ Who is against it and why
✅ Why I think Division III should adopt it
✅ What to ask coaches before your child signs

📋 Is your family 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆? The scorecard is 10 yes or no questions and takes about five minutes. You also get a free seven-day parent action plan.

Encourage your athlete to watch a full game with a coach and evaluate what happens between the highlights. Look at positioning, communication, defensive effort, and decision-making. Understanding those details can help your athlete improve.
 
Go to my bio, then visit keithmondillo.com for the free 10-question Parent Scorecard and 7-Day Parent Action Plan.

📘 Want to know how roster congestion affects your child? Start with 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁’𝘀 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲, 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳 𝗘𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝟱 𝗖𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗹 𝟵𝟯 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗙𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀. Link in my bio or visit KeithMondillo.com.

Day 17 of 30 Days of Recruiting Truth.

Your child’s competition for a roster spot could be a 22-year-old transfer. 👇

Division I and Division II have adopted five-year eligibility. Division III hasn’t, and delegates take it up in January. Rosters are connected, so 𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 reaches every level.

What to do as a senior:

⏳ 𝗖𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘆 𝘄𝗮𝗶𝘁 on high school classes
💪 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆-𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿𝘀 have the edge
❓ 𝗔𝘀𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 how many players at your position have eligibility left

Start earlier. Build a list with real range. Congestion is real, but it’s not a reason to panic. ✅

📘 Get the chapter on roster congestion in 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁’𝘀 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲, 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳 𝗘𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝟱 𝗖𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗹 𝟵𝟯 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗙𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀. Link in my bio or visit KeithMondillo.com.

Ask your athlete's high school or club coach for an honest evaluation of their college potential. Discuss strengths, areas to improve, and appropriate competitive levels. That information can help your family build a more realistic recruiting plan.
 
Go to my bio, then visit keithmondillo.com for the free 10-question Parent Scorecard and 7-Day Parent Action Plan.

📋 Want help wrapping up your recruiting? Start with my book 𝗗𝗼𝗻’𝘁 𝗣𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗼𝗹: 𝗔 𝟳-𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗚𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁-𝗔𝘁𝗵𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗖𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗲. Link in my bio or visit KeithMondillo.com.

Day 16 of 30 Days of Recruiting Truth.

A school’s roster can show you where your child really fits, and it costs nothing to read. 👇

The transfer portal has made rosters change every year. Now five years of eligibility is adding to it. Division I and Division II have adopted it, and Division III votes in January.

Open the roster on the school’s athletic website and look at three things:

📅 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘀 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀: how many players are at your child’s position, and who graduates?
📊 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗵: is it stacked with underclassmen, or is there room?
🔍 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵’𝘀 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻: compare the last two or three rosters. Who’s gone? How many came from high school and how many are transfers?

Do this for every school on your list. ✅

📋 Ready to choose the right school? Get my book 𝗗𝗼𝗻’𝘁 𝗣𝗶𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗼𝗹: 𝗔 𝟳-𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗚𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁-𝗔𝘁𝗵𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗖𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗲. Link in my bio or visit KeithMondillo.com.

👇 Comment the word parent and I’ll send you the information on the Parents’ Recruiting Survival Guide: Avoid the 5 Critical Mistakes That Derail 93% of Families.

I left my team for the first time in 32 years to be at a private Mass in St. Peter’s Basilica and an audience with Pope Leo. 🏀⛪

My players said, “Coach, you have to go.” Yes, I was in the same room as the Pope. 🇮🇹

If your child wants to play in college, ask about the part that comes after the last game. Most athletes play four years or less, and they’ll be alumni for the rest of their lives. 📍

If your child gets hurt, or the coach leaves, or playing time doesn’t come, is this still a school where they’d want to be?

👇 Comment the word parent and I’ll send it to you.

A coach may be evaluating other players, managing roster needs, or working through a busy schedule. Your athlete can respond by following up professionally and continuing to contact appropriate programs. Avoid making decisions based on one unanswered email.
